transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Seaworthy - Head of Infra), Aisha Khan (Seaworthy - Platform Eng), Rahul Sharma (Seaworthy - Security Lead)

Summary:
Jordan: thanks for taking the time, we'll run through how Redwood Private can sit inside your VPCs and what the networking options look like, especially peering vs private endpoints
Carlos: yep, looking to understand network footprint, IP requirements, and any firewall changes

00:00 Jordan: ok kick off, quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, I'm the AE, Priya is our platform SE who does the deep network and infra stuff (laughs a little), over to you folks for quick intros
00:18 Carlos: Carlos here, i run infra at Seaworthy we have a hybrid cloud model, prod in us-east-1 and backup region in us-west-2, on aws, we've got fairly strict egress controls and a shared services VPC
00:32 Aisha: aisha platform eng, mostly focused on k8s, service mesh, and how the inference endpoints will be accessed by our apps
00:45 Rahul: rahul security, interested in encryption, kms, audit logs, and ensuring no data leaves our network unencrypted
00:52 Priya: great, thanks. quick framing: Redwood Private can be deployed with a private control plane or a customer-managed control plane depending on requirements. Networking-wise we commonly support two patterns: VPC peering or PrivateLink/Private Endpoints. each has tradeoffs

01:15 Priya: VPC peering is simple IP routing between VPCs; low latency, but it requires non-overlapping CIDRs and scales poorly for many VPCs. Also peering is regional unless you use transit gateway to do cross-region routing
01:40 Jordan: right, and PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives you an ENI-based private endpoint in your VPC, works well with strict egress rules since connections originate from your VPC to us over ENIs and you can control SGs
01:58 Carlos: ok so peering might be easiest but we have overlapping ranges in some accounts, we use 10.0.0.0/8 in several places for legacy reasons
02:10 Priya: that's a common blocker. if CIDR overlap exists we often recommend PrivateLink or sit the Redwood service in your shared services VPC and route via TGW. PrivateLink avoids routing conflicts but can complicate egress and scaling
02:28 Aisha: curious about IP requirements, how many IPs does Redwood need for the endpoints? we can't spare huge ranges
02:35 Priya: good question. For PrivateLink, each interface endpoint uses a few ENIs per AZ; it's modest, typically tens of IPs per AZ for medium workloads. If you run dedicated GPU clusters in your VPC for private deployment we need a node pool IPs for each instance plus load balancers; we can provide sizing guidance based on expected QPS
02:55 Jordan: can we get you some example numbers after we see your QPS and concurrency? we'll size it. also Redwood supports NAT egress via customer's NAT gateway so outbound model downloads and telemetry can be routed through your egress
03:12 Rahul: we have an outbound firewall that blocks unknown endpoints; would we need to open to specific Redwood IP ranges? concern.. we need to tie this to our SOC2 controls
03:22 Priya: for hosted model downloads, yes you'll allow specific S3 endpoints or IP ranges; for Private deployments, most traffic stays within your VPC, but control plane calls may go to Redwood's management plane depending on the deployment model. we support an air-gapped option for stricter compliance but that's heavier lift
03:41 Carlos: about cross-region, our primary cluster in us-east-1, DR in us-west-2, latency between regions matters for KV cache hits - how do you recommend handling model KV and caching across regions
03:55 Priya: we typically colocate serving in the same region as the primary workload. for cross-region reads, we can route to the nearest region fallback, but that increases latency. Another pattern is to replicate model shards into both regions which increases cost but reduces tail latency
04:20 Jordan: mention of routing policies: Redwood can be configured to route by latency or cost tier; for your SLOs we can pin production traffic to us-east and use us-west for canary or DR

04:42 Aisha: what about certificates and private certs? can we use our own internal PKI for TLS between services
04:50 Priya: yes, mTLS and customer-managed certs supported for Private deployments. we integrate with customer KMS for key management; audit logs are forwarded to your SIEM via an ELK or CloudWatch integration
05:05 Rahul: KMS integration, does Redwood store keys or do we manage them? full control required
05:10 Priya: you manage keys in your KMS; Redwood can use customer KMS for encrypting at rest. for control plane interactions, we can integrate with STS roles and short-lived credentials

05:30 Jordan: quick note on scaling: Dedicated pools can be provisioned in your VPC, autoscaling controlled via our autoscale policies but you'll want permissive IAM for spin up, and appropriate security group rules
05:45 Carlos: any special route table changes? we run strict NACLs
05:50 Priya: route table updates are minimal for PrivateLink; for peering you'll add routes between VPCs/TGW. NACLs need to allow the ENI traffic ranges. We provide a deployment runbook with exact rules
06:08 Aisha: is there a console or dashboard we can access privately to see usage/latency per route
06:14 Jordan: yes, Redwood Console can be deployed with private access or tunneled via SSO; we've done dedicated console instances or SAML/SSO through your IdP for private tenants

06:30 Rahul: audit logs retention — we need 7 years for some workflows. can redwood retain logs or forward to our storage
06:38 Priya: we forward audit logs to your CloudWatch/S3 for long-term retention; we also keep short-term in our console for UI, but long-term archival should be customer-managed

06:50 Jordan: ok want to talk about next steps? we'd like your VPC diagram and CIDRs, traffic profile (RPS, avg tokens per call), and security requirements. we'll run a small connectivity POC to validate PrivateLink + endpoint config
07:05 Carlos: timeline wise we aim to pilot in 4 weeks if network checks out. procurement involved later but security sign-off first
07:12 Priya: action items — we'll send a recommended peering vs PrivateLink doc, and a runbook with SG/NACL examples. Also we'll propose a small pilot: 2 AZs, interface endpoints in us-east-1, a test routing table and security group, and validation steps

07:35 Jordan: any competitors or existing vendors we should be aware of?
07:40 Carlos: our security team mentioned Bedrock and a recent eval of self-hosted inference. Running in VPC matters to them
07:48 Jordan: noted
